goal: Implement External Executor Discovery v1 as a bounded executor-selection support capability without adding an agent, scheduler, authority, or generation path.
acceptance_criteria: Local implementation and approved skill checks precede network discovery.
GitHub, PyPI, and deps.dev adapters are HTTPS allowlisted, bounded, timeout-limited, and optional.
Only a fact-verified, compatible, versioned candidate with a passing isolated bounded trial can become SelectedExecutor.
Archived, deprecated, license-blocked, security-blocked, incompatible, partial-metadata, or failed-trial candidates cannot be selected.
All candidates exhausted or all sources unavailable produces an explicit Agent Build fallback rather than a project blocker.
Eligible capability planning consumes discovery through the existing external WorkNode executor type; ProviderJob remains the sole project-work concurrency unit.
Discovery owns no requirement, planning, scheduling, evidence, acceptance, packaging, delivery, or publication authority.

quality_metrics.measure: unbounded HTTP responses, candidate sets, trial count, subprocess duration, or inherited secrets
quality_metrics.method: offline deterministic unit tests and source inspection

quality_metrics.measure: SelectedExecutor records missing exact version, adequate metadata, policy clearance, or trial PASS
new agents, schedulers, executor types, or formal authorities
quality_metrics.method: kernel contract and architecture regression tests

prevention: Keep discovery deterministic, bounded, allowlisted, support-only, and separate from Provider scheduling
assurance: Cover local and skill priority, source normalization, fact policy, trial isolation, fallback, and WorkNode projection
control: Run scoped discovery, capability, WorkNode, kernel, version, and formal quick checks before canonical publication
improvement: Use one provider-free real lightweight live smoke to expose metadata and trial assumptions

interface_expectations: Capability Strategy supplies bounded capability intent without becoming a search authority
WorkNode external remains the existing executor type and ProviderJob remains the sole concurrency unit
Only selected executors may reach generated dependency materialization and Provider integration context
Provider, formal evidence, local_packager, public delivery, and canonical repository publication authorities remain unchanged
evidence_refs: 124 scoped discovery, capability, WorkNode, skill, generation-lane, project-plan, kernel-contract, and release-version tests passed
provider-free live smoke selected av==19.0.1 from PyPI/deps.dev after GitHub discovery and completed an isolated API trial in 79.07 seconds
formal quick: TIMEOUT at the bounded 300-second limit with no scoped failure attribution

feedback: External discovery now executes through the existing capability-to-WorkNode seam with deterministic policy, isolated trials, explicit Agent Build fallback, and zero Provider calls.
Repository-global formal quick remains unevaluated because the bounded profile timed out; this does not convert the scoped support capability into formal delivery evidence.

worked: Reusing the existing external WorkNode type and ProviderJob boundary avoided a new agent, scheduler, executor type, or authority.
Mocked source adapters made network and policy behavior deterministic while one live smoke exposed the real PyPI/deps.dev/trial path.
Failing closed on partial metadata prevented popular GitHub repositories from becoming selected merely because of stars.
did_not_work: The first live result stopped retaining lower-ranked candidates after selection; the loop was corrected to preserve the bounded candidate set without running more trials.
The repository formal quick profile did not complete within its 300-second bound.
experiments: Measure source latency and cache only immutable metadata facts in a future version without weakening revalidation or selection policy.
